title: Fourier decomposition by support
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $(b_j)_{j\in\iota}$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with $b_{j_0}$ the constant-one function for some $j_0\in\iota$, and with $mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}[b_j(x)b_k(x)]$ equal to $1$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise. For every natural number $n$ and every real-valued function $f$ on $n$-tuples from $\Omega$, the sum, over all subsets $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, of the Fourier components of $f$ whose multi-indices differ from $j_0$ exactly on $J$ equals $f$.
hypotheses_covered: a basis vector is constant one
basis is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$
